about: The compound's public bathroom (compound.json units id "bath", PUBLIC BATHROOM): a 20 ft container painted teal on a 300 mm fieldstone plinth, beside the galley in the study room's row, its front facing north toward the courtyard. The founder's brief: two toilet rooms, two hand basins and a urinal, sizes assumed, not given (D-022). It serves everyone without a bathroom of their own: the campers in the tents, guests at the bar lounge and the fire pit in the evening, at the volleyball and in the study room by day (guide/operations.md), and the team, as the office, the bar and the galley have none; the studios and the guest rooms have their own (D-029). The outside follows the homepage model (scripts/site/render/compound.html): one door and two high windows in the front. The fittings stand in one row against the back wall, west to east: the two toilet rooms, the urinal room, then the basins straight across from the door, which sits at the east end of the front wall (the homepage model puts it mid-front; it moves here). A corridor along the front wall, under the two windows, joins them. The 2D (public-bathroom-plan.tsx) and the 3D (scripts/site/render/public-bathroom.html) both read this file. Plan in metres, seen from the courtyard and mirrored as the homepage draws the compound (D-022): x to the right from the west end (the galley's side), y toward the courtyard (north), the container's centre line at y = 0; heights above the container's underside unless stated. Every size inside is a design choice, not yet sourced [A], and the plan is not yet checked against Rwanda's rules for public toilets. Revised 2026-10-31 to this one-row layout (D-060); the 2D, the 3D and the plumbing and electric runs all follow it.

container.about: ISO 20 ft, outside, painted teal as on the homepage, on a fieldstone plinth 300 mm high and 100 mm proud all round. The owner's brief (D-029) asks for timber cladding and 40 x 60 cm block stands under the corner castings; the cladding kit is still to be designed, so the shell stays as the homepage draws it until it is. The homepage draws no cargo doors on this box: whichever end has them, they stay shut and are lined over [A]. Linings and tiles leave 5.86 x 2.2 m inside [A]; the floor and ceiling heights are above the container's underside, so the floor stands about 0.45 m above the ground.

front.about: The north wall: the door at its east end, from 4.95 to 5.85 m, and two windows from 0.4 to 0.9 and 1.7 to 2.2 m, measured from the west end. The homepage model draws the door mid-front, from 3.0 to 3.9 m; it moves to the end so the fittings can stand in one row with the basins facing it. The door: red steel with a glass panel in its upper half, in a red frame, hinged at its east jamb and opening in, so it stands back against the east end wall, on a closer [A]; the glass obscured [A]. The windows: white frames with a middle bar, sill 1.3 m and head 2.0 m above the container's underside (about 1.15 m above the floor inside), lighting the corridor; obscured glass, top-hung sashes that open for air [A].

entry.about: The homepage draws no step up to the door. Here a fieldstone landing at the plinth's height, 1.5 m wide and 1.0 m out from the wall, centred on the door, so it runs a little past the east end, and one step 0.35 m deep down to the grass, both under a concrete cap like the fire pit's: risers of 150, 150 and 160 mm up to the door sill. A wall light over the door, on with the path lights from 18:00 (guide/operations.md). All [A].

partitions.about: Timber studs lined both sides in cement board, 100 mm, floor to ceiling, tiled and painted like the walls [A]: along the front of the row with its three doors, between the two toilet rooms, between the second room and the urinal room, and on the urinal room's east side, where the row meets the basins.

finishes.about: Non-slip floor tiles in warm grey falling to a floor drain, white wall tiles to 1.5 m above the floor and off-white paint above, on the walls and the partitions alike; the doors, the counter and the cupboard in the studio's Medium Oak, sealed (D-028 keeps the studio's interior); white ceramic fittings and chrome taps. Ceiling lights in every room on motion sensors, so they go off when nobody is in. All [A].

toilets.about: The two toilet rooms side by side at the west end of the row, against the back wall: 1.35 m wide and 1.2 m deep inside, without a window of their own (the corridor has the two) [A]. Open to everyone, each locked from inside by an indicator bolt that staff can open from outside [A]; a women's and a men's side instead is the founder's call. Each WC is floor-standing with a close-coupled cistern, against the back wall, its centre 0.35 m from the room's west wall, facing the door and reaching 0.65 m into the room, a roll holder on the west wall beside it [A]. The doors, 0.7 m, open in off the corridor and stand back against the east wall, clear of the WC [A].

passage.about: The corridor along the front wall, under the two windows: 0.9 m wide, from the lobby at the east end past the three doors of the row to the cleaner's cupboard at its west end.

cupboard.about: The cleaner's cupboard at the corridor's dead end, against the west end wall and stopping at the first window's jamb: full height, 0.3 m deep and 0.9 m wide, two doors opening along the corridor; a mop and bucket on the floor and shelves above for paper, soap and cleaning things, for housekeeping (guide/operations.md) [A]. It has no tap: the bucket is filled at a basin [A].

lobby.about: Inside the door, at the east end: the full depth of the box from the row's end to the end wall, the basins on its back wall straight across from the door and the towels on the end wall. Its floor falls to a drain, so it can be washed down [A].

basins.about: The two hand basins, shared by everyone, at the east end of the back wall, straight across from the door, so everyone passes them on the way out: white bowls on a 1.4 m counter on black steel brackets, open below so the floor washes clean, after the studio's basin console; push taps that close themselves, one soap dispenser between the bowls and a long mirror over the counter. The counter top 0.85 m above the floor. All [A].

towels.about: A paper towel dispenser on the east end wall beside the counter, a lidded bin under it [A]: x is the wall, y the dispenser's centre.

urinal.about: The urinal in a small room of its own in the row, between the second toilet room and the basins, 0.9 x 1.2 m inside, so nobody at the basins sees it; its door opens in off the corridor and stands back against the room's east wall, clear of the urinal. A wall urinal on the back wall, its rim about 0.6 m above the floor, and a small extract fan high on the same wall, as this room has no window. All [A].

drains.about: Every fitting drains under the floor and out through the back of the plinth to an inspection chamber (IC1) behind the back wall, then on to the farm's septic tank and soakaway, which takes the farm's WCs and basins (guide/operations.md); the runs are in plumbing below [A].

accessible.about: Considered, and not drawn. A wheelchair toilet room needs about 1.5 x 2.2 m clear inside and a door of 0.9 m or more opening out (the common minimum, for example the UK's Approved Document M; Rwanda's own rule is not yet checked). In this box it fits only by taking the whole west end and planning the rest round it: the lobby beside it, the other toilet room and the urinal room sharing the east end, no cleaner's cupboard and no window for that toilet room. And with the floor about 0.45 m above the ground, level access needs a ramp about 5.4 m long at 1 in 12, which the compound plan does not have. Whether one of the two rooms becomes accessible, with its ramp, is the founder's call.

showers.about: D-022 lists no shower, so none is drawn. The tents have no washing of their own, and the power guide plans a solar water heater on this building (guide/trades/power.md), so whether the bathroom takes one or two showers for the camping guests is an open question. A shower room needs about the space of a toilet room here (the studio's tray is 1.0 x 0.9 m, D-026), so one would replace a fitting of the brief or go in a second building [A].

plumbing.about: The bathroom's water, in the studio's conventions (guide/trades/plumber.md, public/designs/studio/data/pipes.csv): PP-R PN20 for the supply, 25 mm for the main and 20 mm inside, run in the lining 300 mm above the floor, then straight up to each outlet; uPVC drains under the floor in the plinth, falling at least 1:40, with a rodding eye at every bend; a 75 mm open vent; every pipe pressure-tested at 10 bar for an hour before the tiles go on. Cold only: the basins are cold, as the studio's (D-053), and nothing here needs hot water until a shower is added (see showers; guide/trades/power.md plans a solar water heater on this building). The main comes from the farm's tank and booster pump at 2.5 to 3 bar, as the studio's; the stop valve, filter and meter sit in the cleaner's cupboard, where only staff reach them. The soil line leaves IC1 for the farm's septic tank and soakaway, which site.json places at least 50 m from the borehole; that tank was sized for the two studios (public/designs/studio/data/site-water.csv) and must be re-sized for the campers, the bar and the fire pit, whose numbers are not set [U]. Points: x, y in plan metres; z in metres above the finished floor (negative: under it, in the plinth). Every run and size is a design choice for the plumber to confirm [A].

electric.about: The bathroom's power, in the studio's conventions (public/designs/studio/data/circuits.csv): a feeder from the farm's site board (guide/trades/power.md) to a small lockable unit board in the lobby, on the urinal room's east partition above head height, a main switch, surge protection and one 30 mA type A RCBO for each circuit, TT earthing on the building's own rod. Every run goes up into the ceiling void, along it and straight down to its device. The lights are LED ceiling lights with a motion sensor built in, so each room lights when someone walks in and goes dark after a few minutes (finishes); the urinal room's extract fan runs with its light and for 15 minutes after. The light over the door is on a photocell and time switch in the board, on with the path lights from 18:00 (guide/operations.md). One socket in the corridor by the cupboard, for the cleaner. A spare way waits for a shower heater or a hand dryer, should the founder add either. Points: x, y in plan metres; z in metres above the finished floor. Every device, rating and size is a design choice for the electrician to confirm [A]; the feeder's size waits for the site board's design.
